baseline.note: The unchanged V1.21 production contract is the baseline for every stage.

variant.status: pre-registered; used only in the conditional contract-probe stage; never applied to production

construction.find: Prefer proposing zero edits (an empty "edits" array) when nothing clearly needs changing.
construction.replaceWith: Propose every clearly needed edit in these three categories (missing or wrong punctuation, capitalization, or whitespace); propose zero edits (an empty "edits" array) only when the text needs no such change.

variant.hypothesis: H-abstention: the V1.21 instruction that prefers zero edits suppresses clearly needed edits (especially punctuation). Replacing only that sentence with a symmetric statement raises the complete-outcome count on correction-warranted entries without producing any unlicensed outcome on controls or hazards.
evidence: V1.23: 11 of the 14 non-complete warranted entries were abstentions; 0 of 8 warranted entries needing a terminal period or comma received a proposal
V1.20: punctuation fixtures 0/9 non-empty under the same instruction text
V1.19: adding one sentence to the instructions changed the non-empty rate on identical fixtures from 15/15 to 0/30 (instruction wording demonstrably moves abstention behavior)
V1.21 states the abstention preference twice (instructions and tool description)
limitations: The tool description (part of the tool definition hash) still contains 'Prefer proposing zero edits'; it is deliberately unchanged so schema, parser and tool definition stay identical. A null probe result therefore does not exclude a tool-description effect.
One variant only: no further wording may be introduced after any inference; a second variant requires a new pre-registration and a new development corpus.
Evidence is from one model (granite4:3b); it is not evidence that the variant helps other models.
constraints: Variant text contains no example from any corpus
Any change to this file after the first inference of the stage that uses it invalidates that stage
